_comment: A world with fire under it, which is four separate things and one word for them: the mountains, the
small craters that shell you in open country, the deep magma nobody sees until they dig into it, and
the tubes seeded through the rock that flood the tunnel you open them with. Each has a page of its own
-- `volcano`, `firespout`, `magma_chamber`, `lava_tubes`, all derived from the placed features -- and
this is the page for wanting the set.
**It admits by name and leans by tag, and it has to be both.** Admitting is what puts something in an
Age: a member reached only by a query is read as a *description* (`Claim.onlyWhereItGrows`), which asks
for more of a thing where it already grows, and none of these four grows anywhere on its own -- no
biome carries them, so a pure tag query would have found them, weighed them and placed nothing. The
lean is what the tag is for: `#molten` also catches vanilla's lava lakes and springs, which DO grow in
biomes, so a volcanic Age gets more of those where it has them without this word naming either.
The cost of naming them is that a fifth molten feature would not be reached until it is added here --
which is exactly what happened when `lava_tubes` was split out of `volcano` on 2026-09-11. That is the
price of `admits` being by name only, which is deliberate: being in the tag table is what puts a member
in the pool, so admitting by tag could never add anything.
**`#molten` reaches far wider than the five features that carry it in `preset_tags`, and that is a fact
about the tag rather than about this word.** It derives from `#fire`, `#soul_fire_base_blocks` and
`is_nether` (the-tag-layer.md), so the lean lands on twenty-two vanilla features -- the lava lakes and
springs and magma that belong here, and soul sand, soul fire, nether gold and quartz that arguably do
not. A volcanic Age comes out nether-flavoured rather than merely fiery. Narrowing it means leaning on
the three by name instead, or a tag narrower than `is_nether` gives; the tag layer already records this
derivation as a rough edge.
**It touches one aspect**, which is the rule `auroral.json` records and `electromagnetic.json` follows:
a narrowing word is priced in its lowest-ordinal aspect, so a climate nudge here would quietly reprice
it as a word about the weather. A writer who wants the heat as well writes `scorching` beside it, and
words composing is how the Art says a compound thing.
It narrows nothing despite its tier: with no `restricts`, no `excludes` and no `chooses` on features,
`constrainsPresetsIn` is false there, so this adds and lifts without striking a single tree.
